title: Northgate Analytics — partner outreach notebook
content:
Quick notebook / scratchpad for Northgate Analytics outreach — keep as my single source of raw thoughts before formalizing proposal.

Goal: qualify fit, land 6–8 week pilot with a single product team (recommendations or search) that shows 30–50% latency reduction or 25% token-cost reduction vs their current hosted model path. Primary hook is predictable inference economics + private deployment option for PII-sensitive queries.

Background notes (from public site + investor deck skim):
- Northgate Analytics: B2B retail analytics, real-time product discovery and personalized recommendations for mid-market retailers. Heavy on embeddings for similarity + re-ranking ML.
- They run a hybrid infra: inference on cloud GPUs (spot instances) + CPU-based microservices for feature joins. Mentions occasional latency spikes during sale events.
- CTO: Lina Morales (LinkedIn verified). Head of ML: Rajiv Menon. Head of Eng: Connor Blake.

Initial hypothesis (why Redwood fits):
- Their pain: unpredictable latency spikes during peak traffic -> lost conversion dollars.
- Redwood value props: dedicated capacity (predictable throughput), smart fallback (cheaper model variant when GPU pool is constrained), cache/kv prefix reuse for repeated queries (common in recommendations), cost controls and tracing that tie token costs to queries.
- Enterprise concern: PII from customer events -> Private deployment/VPC + KMS/HSM integration is a strong differentiator vs public hosted providers.

Stakeholders and mapping (who to win):
- Rajiv (Head of ML) -> cares about model quality, ability to deploy latest open models, quantization options.
- Connor (Head of Eng) -> cares about SLOs, observability, runbooks, dev experience for rollouts.
- Lina (CTO) -> procurement, security/compliance, enterprise contract.
- PM for Recommendations (likely main pilot owner) -> day-to-day user, wants low-risk experiment.

Technical questions to seed in discovery call:
- Current models: which family? Are they using proprietary fine-tuned variants or off-the-shelf LM + embedding stacks?
- Peak QPS and 99th pct latency targets today; what happened during last big sale (numbers)?
- Do they have an existing prefix/KV caching layer or dedupe at the application layer?
- Data residency: Do they require on-prem or is VPC with customer-managed KMS sufficient?
- What metrics define success for them (CTR, conversion rate, revenue per session, latency %)?

Quick outbound subject lines (test 3 variants):
A) Cut recommendation latency 30% during sale spikes — quick pilot?
B) Demo: private, predictable LLM inference for Northgate’s recommendation stack
C) Idea for Rajiv — test a dedicated inference pool for 6 weeks (no infra work from you)

Email A (short, cold):
Hey Rajiv —
I noticed Northgate leans on embeddings + rerank for product discovery. We’ve helped similar teams reduce p99 latency and token spend by combining a dedicated inference pool with KV prefix caching so repeated candidate queries hit the cache instead of regenerating.
Would you be open to a quick 20-min sync to share what we did for a marketplace client and see if it maps to Northgate?
— Maya

Email B (follow-up with value prop + pilot sketch):
Rajiv —
Following up — quick sketch of a low-friction pilot:
- 6 week pilot, one recommendation route behind a Redwood dedicated pool
- We run a small scale canary (1–5% traffic) -> measure p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per 1k queries
- No model retraining required; we can use your existing model weights or a Redwood-verified quantized variant
If that sounds interesting I can send a one-page pilot plan and proposed success metrics.

Call script (first discovery, 20 minutes):
1) 2 min intro + why I’m calling (reference sale event pain)
2) 5 min: ask Rajiv about current infra, models, p99 during peak
3) 5 min: quick sketch of Redwood architecture (dedicated pools, fallback, KV cache) — highlight: rolling upgrades and canaries built-in
4) 5 min: pilot proposal and success metrics (p99 reduction target, cost per thousand tokens)
5) 3 min: next steps (identify PM owner, times for pilot kickoff)

Objection handling (notes / bullet rebuttals):
- "We already have autoscaling and spot pools": autoscaling helps for throughput but not p99 under cold starts and tail latency; dedicated pools + warmed KV cache reduces tail significantly. Cite internal benchmark: 35% p99 improvement vs spot pool for seq len 256 workloads.
- "Security / compliance concerns": Redwood Private can run in your VPC, KMS keys remain yours, audit logs sent to your SIEM. We can do a SOC2 + a quick security questionnaire.
- "Cost unknown / risky": propose fixed budget pilot ($Xk) with a clear measurement period and rollback. Also show estimate: with prefix caching and batching, expected token cost drop 20–40% for typical recommendation patterns.
- "Integration overhead": we provide SDKs and quickstart templates—most pilots need a lightweight routing change and an endpoint key; we handle server-side pooling and observability.

Pilot measurement plan (what success looks like):
- Primary metric: p99 latency reduction on the recommendation route (target: >= 30% improvement within 2 weeks of pilot).
- Secondary metrics: cost per 1k queries (target: <= baseline * 0.8), conversion uplift (if available), error rate.
- Observability: Redwood Console dashboard access + export of token-level traces for correlation with GA events.

Operational checklist (what we need from them):
- Endpoint / route to mirror (path + example payloads)
- Sample traffic trace for 24–72 hrs (or synthetic workload) to simulate batching & cache hit rate
- Contact for security questionnaire / KMS
- Timezone windows and peak traffic window info (for on-call overlap)

Pilot timeline (tentative):
Week 0: alignment + finalize target route + security kickoff
Week 1: infra prep + small canary config (1%)
Week 2: canary -> 5% traffic if metrics good
Week 3–5: ramp and iterate (tune batching, cache TTLs, fallback models)
Week 6: wrap + runbook handoff + exec review (deck)

Pricing sketch to mention (keep high level):
- Dedicated pool: monthly reserved + usage during pilot; we can lean on short-term discount for pilot
- Observability add-on: short retention window during pilot included
- Option to convert to Private (VPC/on-prem) post-pilot if compliance needs require

Notes to self (random todo):
- Pull similar customer case with marketplace (ask Samir for deck) — include concrete numbers (before/after p99, cost delta)
- Add a short gif of Console showing p99 line and token breakdown into the one-pager
- Draft SOW template for 6-week pilot (legal review needed) — loop in Heather in legal
- Find Rajiv’s preferred email (sometimes uses personal on GitHub); prefer intros from existing connections: Connor Blake (eng) -> likely easier path to PM

Possible customization angles to test in outreach A/B:
1) Security-first: lead with Private/VPC and KMS (for enterprises with PII)
2) Cost-first: lead with expected token cost reduction and batching gains
3) Reliability-first: lead with p99 reduction and canary rollouts

Slack/CRM markers (for later tagging):
- add to HubSpot as "northgate - pilot interest" tag + stage: discovery
- Slack note: post summary in #bd-weekly on Monday (include ask: who has similar retail case studies)

Bottom line: aim to get 20-min intro with Rajiv or Connor; if they push procurement, aim to convert to a security sketched pilot with Lina involved. Keep outreach short, but have pilot flow ready to send as one-pager.

-- end of scratchpad --

(keeping this file intentionally messy — will extract to an internal proposal doc if we move to next step)
